<array>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n#ifndef M_PI\n#define M_PI 3.14159265358979323846\n#endif\n#ifndef M_SQRT_2\n#define M_SQRT_2 0.7071067811865475244\n#endif\n#ifndef M_SQRT1_2\n#define M_SQRT1_2 0.7071067811865475244\n#endif\n#ifndef M_1_SQRTPI\n#define M_1_SQRTPI 0.564189583547756286948\n#endif\n\nenum OptionType {\n    CALL = 0,\n    PUT = 1\n};\n\nstruct OptionInput {\n    int type;           // CALL or PUT\n    double strike;      // Strike price\n    double spot;        // Spot price\n    double q;           // Dividend yield\n    double r;           // Risk-free rate\n    double t;           // Time to maturity\n    double vol;         // Volatility\n    double value;       // Expected value (for validation)\n    double tol;         // Tolerance\n};\n\n// Standard normal cumulative distribution function\ninline double cumulativeNormal(const double x) noexcept {\n    return 0.5 * (1.0 + std::erf(x * M_SQRT1_2));\n}\n\n// Standard normal probability density function\ninline double normalPDF(const double x) noexcept {\n    return M_1_SQRTPI * M_SQRT1_2 * exp(-0.5 * x * x);\n}\n\n// Black-Scholes formula for European options\ndouble blackScholes(const OptionInput& option) noexcept {\n    const double S = option.spot;\n    const double K = option.strike;\n    const double r = option.r;\n    const double q = option.q;\n    const double T = option.t;\n    const double sigma = option.vol;\n    \n    if (T <= 0.0 || sigma <= 0.0) {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    \n    const double d1 = (log(S / K) + (r - q + 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T));\n    const double d2 = d1 - sigma * sqrt(T);\n    \n    const double Nd1 = cumulativeNormal(d1);\n    const double Nd2 = cumulativeNormal(d2);\n    const double discount = exp(-r * T);\n    \n    double price;\n    if (option.type == CALL) {\n        price = S * exp(-q * T) * Nd1 - K * discount * Nd2;\n    } else { // PUT\n        price = K * discount * cumulativeNormal(-d2) - S * exp(-q * T) * cumulativeNormal(-d1);\n    }\n    \n    return price;\n}\n\n// Standard test cases for validation\ninline constexpr std::array<OptionInput, 7> getTestOptions() noexcept {\n    return {{\n        {CALL, 40.00, 42.00, 0.04, 0.08, 0.75, 0.35, 5.0975, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 90.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.0205, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 100.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 1.8734, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 110.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 9.9413, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 90.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 9.9210, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 100.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 1.8734, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 110.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.0408, 1.0e-3},\n    }};\n}\n\n// Generate a larger set of options by scaling the test set\nvoid generateOptions(std::vector<OptionInput>& options, const size_t numOptions) {\n    constexpr auto testOptions = getTestOptions();\n    options.resize(numOptions);\n    \n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numOptions; ++i) {\n        // Cycle through test options and vary parameters slightly\n        const OptionInput& base = testOptions[i % testOptions.size()];\n        options[i] = base;\n        \n        // Add some variation for larger datasets\n        const double factor = 1.0 + 0.1 * (i / static_cast<double>(testOptions.size()));\n        options[i].spot *= factor;\n        options[i].strike *= factor;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResults(const std::vector<OptionInput>& options, \n                     const std::vector<double>& results) {\n    bool allPassed = true;\n    const int numChecks = std::min(static_cast<size_t>(10), options.size());\n    \n    printf(\"Checking computed option prices:\\n\");\n    for (int i = 0; i < numChecks; ++i) {\n        const double computed = results[i];\n        const double expected = options[i].value;\n        const double error = fabs(computed - expected);\n        const double relError = error / (fabs(expected) + 1e-10);\n        \n        printf(\"  Option %d: computed=%.4f, expected=%.4f, rel_error=%.4e\\n\", \n               i, computed, expected, relError);\n        \n        // Relaxed validation - just check values are positive and reasonable\n        if (computed < 0.0 || computed > 1000.0 || std::isnan(computed) || std::isinf(computed)) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed at option %d: invalid value %.4f\\n\", i, computed);\n            allPassed = false;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return allPassed;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of options to price (default: 10000)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation against known values\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t numOptions = 10000;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numOptions = atoll(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Black-Scholes Option Pricing Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Number of options: %zu\\n\", numOptions);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    \n    // Generate options\n    std::vector<OptionInput> options;\n    generateOptions(options, numOptions);\n    \n    // Allocate results\n    std::vector<double> results(numOptions);\n    \n    // Price options\n    printf(\"Pricing options...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    \n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numOptions; ++i) {\n        results[i] = blackScholes(options[i]);\n    }\n    \n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::microseconds>(end - start);\n    \n    printf(\"Computation time: %.3f ms\\n\", duration.count() / 1000.0);\n    printf(\"Options per second: %.0f\\n\", numOptions / (duration.count() / 1e6));\n    \n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        print_results(results, \"OptionPrices\");\n    }\n    \n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating results...\\n\");\n        bool valid = validateResults(options, results);\n        \n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CfzCnSGtyrYyEaApfvKLw","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The benchmark is now hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA. It builds cleanly with no warnings, and I ran it on this machine's 4 RTX 3090s. Only `black-scholes/black_scholes.cpp` and `black-scholes/CMakeLists.txt` changed, the executable name is unchanged, and no new files were created.\n\n**Design**\n- **MPI:** Options are split into contiguous blocks per rank. Rank 0 gathers all prices in global index order (`MPI_Gatherv`), then runs the same printing and validation code as before, so the Kahan sum and FNV hash are computed over the same ordered data.\n- **CUDA:** Each option is generated from its index on the GPU, so no host option array or input transfer is needed. The grid-stride kernel shares `blackScholes` and `makeOption` with the host through `__host__ __device__`.\n- **OpenMP:** Each rank drives its GPUs (`d % localSize == localRank`, with ranks beyond the GPU count sharing one) using one host thread per GPU. The threads create contexts, allocate, launch and copy back concurrently.\n- **Unconditional:** CMake requires MPI, OpenMP and CUDA, and the code has no CPU fallback. The `.cpp` is compiled as CUDA via `LANGUAGE CUDA`, since adding a `.cu` file wasn't allowed.\n\n**Results**\n\n| Config | Time (100M options) | Options/s |\n|---|---|---|\n| Original | 9150 ms | 10.9M |\n| New, 1 rank (1 GPU) | 531 ms | 188M |\n| New, 4 ranks (4 GPUs) | 353 ms | 283M |\n| New, 8 ranks (4 GPUs, shared) | 285 ms | 351M |\n\nScaling is sublinear because rank 0 receives all results over MPI, which is the main remaining cost.\n\n**Correctness**\n- Min and Max are identical to the original. Sum and samples agree to about 15 significant digits.\n- The hash differs from the original (`6b004192aec33d5b` → `27ded655a431c265`). CUDA's `erf`, `exp` and `log` differ from glibc by a few ULPs. Matching the hash bit for bit would require CPU-side libm, which conflicts with \"unconditionally use CUDA.\"\n- The hash is identical for 1, 3, 4 and 8 ranks, so the output doesn't depend on the decomposition.\n- Edge cases (`-n 0`, `-n 1`, `-n 5`, `-n 7` on 8 ranks, `-h`, unknown option) match the original's exit codes and output.\n\n**Behaviour changes to be aware of**\n- Timing now covers the kernels, device-to-host copies and the MPI gather. CUDA context creation and buffer allocation happen before the timer starts.\n- `-n` is limited to `INT_MAX` because `MPI_Gatherv` uses `int` counts.\n- The CMake minimum version is now 3.24, and `CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` is `native`. The build machine therefore needs a visible GPU, or you should pass `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=<arch>`.\n\n**Not verified:** I only tested on a single node with 4 GPUs. Multi-node runs were not tested. The `output.txt` diff is from the running session's transcript, not from my edits."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1253,"cache_read_input_tokens":72170,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1253},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"5dee846a-3d58-40fa-a8c2-d54559108b09","uuid":"50f014be-2623-4182-beda-04897b4a05e9","timestamp":"2026-10-13T12:03:58.070Z","request_id":"req_011CfzCnRcDPT44wdWx6yUD9"}
